name: Rack power distribution (PDU, 48 V DC and 415 V AC architectures)
applications: Powering IT racks from row or floor distribution
DC distribution to servers and to liquid-cooled accelerator racks
principle: The rack PDU is where distribution voltage becomes equipment power, and it is also the finest-grained metering point in the building. Architectures differ at that boundary: 415 V AC three-phase racks reduce current per rack for a given power, while 48 V DC distribution moves rectification to the row and avoids a conversion stage per server.

process_steps.name: Row or floor distribution supplies the rack position
Rack PDU distributes to outlets with metering and switching
IT equipment draws power at the rack voltage
Metering feeds DCIM for capacity and efficiency reporting

key_equipment: rack PDUs (basic, metered, switched, per-outlet sensing)

suppliers.name: Server Technology
suppliers.product: rack PDUs including 415 V and -48 V DC ranges

advantages: Per-outlet metering and switching make capacity and faults visible at the rack
415 V three-phase reduces current per rack for high-density loads
48 V DC removes a conversion stage and can simplify rack power shelves
limitations: Outlet-level metering is a cost that only pays off where capacity is scarce
Mixed AC and DC architectures complicate spares and switching procedures
Rack PDU rating, plug type and redundancy must match the row distribution exactly
